thread:
incident-bot: P0 alert — continuous-batching latency cliff observed in us-west-2. 95th token latency spike -> 2.8s (baseline ~120ms). KV cache evictions also spiking. Paging oncall. @maya you're up.

maya (oncall): seeing it. metrics link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/cont-batch/concurrency-vortex?orgId=1 -> queue length + inflight microbatches really jumped around 10:03 UTC.

sam (eng-runtime): looks like microbatch size distribution jumped. avg_microbatch_size went from ~6 -> ~42 at high conc. Also observe large prefix cache churn: kvcache_evictions_per_minute ~ 38k.

kevin (sre): any deploys around that time?

ops-bot: deploybot: rollout finished for model-serving/continuous-batch v1.12.3 @ 10:00:27 UTC (sha abc123).

maya (oncall): deploy at 10:00 is suspicious. sam, is v1.12.3 known to change batching heuristics?

sam (eng-runtime): v1.12.3 tweaks to batching heuristics + a small change to prefix caching TTL (it was supposed to be opt-in but default flipped for some routes). Could cause more cache entries to be kept but also more churn under concurrency.

lia (support): customers A and B reporting higher latencies and some 504s. Lia has initial impact list: customer-A (prod) — 5% 504s last 15m; customer-B (staging) — degraded throughput.

maya (oncall): triage plan: 1) apply immediate ingress throttling at edge to drop nonessential low-priority traffic, 2) reduce max_microbatch_size on affected nodepool, 3) revert the TTL flip or force a short TTL, 4) if needed, route heavy customers to dedicated nodes. I'll coordinate.

sam (eng-runtime): commands ready. we can hotpatch runtime via admin API. Example to lower max microbatch:

```
# set max_microbatch_size from 64 -> 16 on pool continuous-usw2-1
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.local/policies/continuous-usw2-1 -d '{"max_microbatch_size":16}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

maya (oncall): executing step 2 now.

maya (oncall): done — lowered max_microbatch_size to 16 on continuous-usw2-1. Applying jitter tighten to avoid synchronized flushes. setting jitter_rate to 0.15 -> 0.05.

ops-bot: configchange: continuous-usw2-1 updated (max_microbatch_size=16, jitter=0.05) by maya at 10:06:02 UTC.

sam (eng-runtime): pushing a TTL change to kvcache for prefix policy. set prefix_ttl_seconds=30 (was 300) for the model routes that opted into the flip.

kevin (sre): applying ingress token-bucket throttle: burst=500, rate=200/s for non-dedicated routes.

ops-bot: networkpolicy: ingress throttle applied to route /v1/generate (non-dedicated) by kevin at 10:07:14 UTC.

lia (support): initial customer notes: latency @customer-A 95p dropped from 2.8s -> 900ms after changes, 504s down to 0.8%. Good early signs.

sam (eng-runtime): interesting metric: microbatch tail size dropped to 12 at high conc after max_microbatch change. kvcache_evictions_per_minute trending down.

maya (oncall): good. next steps: 1) keep throttles until we confirm stability for 30m, 2) prepare rollback of v1.12.3 if metrics regress once load ramps, 3) draft customer postmortem and impact summary. Lia, can you collect support tickets/correlate request_ids for customers with 504s?

lia (support): on it. ticketing note: we should proactively email customers A/B with mitigation steps and ETA for root cause.

sam (eng-runtime): for long-term: revert the default TTL flip, add a safeguard so that kvcache entry churn > X triggers an autoswitch to conservative cache policy. I can open a PR.

kevin (sre): also recommend adding a soft circuit-breaker on microbatch growth: if avg_microbatch_size over 1m > 20 and queue_length > N then enforce microbatch cap and drain.

maya (oncall): Agreed. For now, keep the temporary throttles and microbatch cap. I'll handoff to kevin in 20m for monitoring window closure.

kevin (sre): taking over monitoring at 10:20 UTC. If any regression during my watch I'll escalate to oncall lead.

ops-bot: alert: regression_check scheduled in 10m.

lia (support): customer impact summary for comms (short): "We observed increased latencies and intermittent request failures due to a batching/cache interaction in a recent runtime deploy. We've applied throttles and configuration changes to mitigate; we're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a root cause and timeline."

maya (oncall): adding follow-up items: create blocked-PR label for rollback tests, add e2e with concurrency fuzzing, add metric alert for kvcache_evictions_per_minute > 10k for >5m.

sam (eng-runtime): captured logs for affected pods:
```
[10:03:15] warn: microbatch flush timeout triggered (inflight 512)
[10:03:16] error: kvcache eviction loop: prefix="user:.*" evictions=1200/sec
[10:03:18] warn: queuing delay 450ms for request_id=xyz
```

maya (oncall): thanks. Handoff note to kevin: watch for any new 5xx spikes and customer A token ids; contact support if >1% 504s in 15m.

kevin (sre): acknowledged. I'll keep the loop here and update.

incident-bot: P0 status -> mitigated (controls in place, active monitoring). last update at 10:20:20 UTC.

kevin (sre): closing handoff — continuing monitoring. will create an internal incident timeline doc and link when ready.
